anthropic.no_limit_found: None of the official sources I checked sets a hard limit on the NUMBER of files in a skill folder. Sources checked: the platform.claude.com Agent Skills overview, Skill authoring best practices, the Skills API guide and the Create Skill API reference, the Claude Code skills docs, the agentskills.io specification, the claude.ai support article on creating custom skills, the Anthropic engineering blog, and the skill-creator SKILL.md. None of them requires markdown-only files either. The spec says a skill 'may contain any files and directories beyond the required SKILL.md'. The overview says 'No practical limit on bundled content'. skill-creator calls bundled resources 'unlimited'. Hard limits found: (1) Skills API / Claude Platform: 'Maximum Skill upload size: 30 MB (all files combined, uncompressed)'. (2) Frontmatter: name is at most 64 characters and description at most 1024 characters. The API display_name is at most 255 characters. In Claude Code, the combined description and when_to_use text is cut to 1,536 characters in the skill listing. (3) 'Maximum Skills per request: 20' in the API. This caps skills per API request, not files per skill, and may be where the '20' idea came from. Soft guidance (not enforced): keep the SKILL.md body under 500 lines (best practices, Claude Code docs, spec), and the spec recommends under 5,000 tokens. The Level 2 instructions are 'Under 5k tokens'. Add a table of contents to reference files over 100 lines (best practices) or over 300 lines (skill-creator). Runtime limits that matter for bundled scripts: API skills run with no network access and no runtime package installation. I could not find a claude.ai zip upload size limit in the support article.

openai.no_limit_found:
No official OpenAI source sets a 20-file cap or requires skill files to be markdown. Only SKILL.md is required. Hard limits on file count do exist, but only on specific platforms, and they are far higher than 20:
(1) OpenAI API skills (Responses API): up to 500 files per skill version, a 50 MB zip upload and 25 MB uncompressed (developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-skills).
(2) Skills imported from an MCP server during plugin submission: up to 100 files per skill; SKILL.md up to 256 KiB; each supporting file up to 1 MiB; all resources for one skill up to 5 MiB; archives per scan up to 8 MiB; up to 5 skills per scan (developers.openai.com/plugins/build/mcp-server).
(3) Local Codex/ChatGPT skills (learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills; developers.openai.com/codex/skills now 308-redirects there): no file-count or size limit is documented. The only budget is on the initial skills list, capped at 2% of the context window or 8,000 characters, and it does not limit what a skill folder holds.
The official validator (skill-creator/scripts/quick_validate.py) checks only the frontmatter: name up to 64 characters, description up to 1024 characters with no angle brackets, and allowed keys. It does not check file count or file type.
Soft guidance: SKILL.md body under 500 lines or under 5k words; bundled resources are described as 'Unlimited'; references stay one level deep; add a table of contents to reference files over 100 lines; add grep patterns for files over 10k words.
Caveat: the openai/skills repo README now says it is deprecated in favor of openai/plugins and the Build plugins guide. The skill-creator guidance quoted above comes from that deprecated repo, though the current docs repeat the same structure.
My own count, not a quote: in the local clone of openai/plugins (commit 1dc1958, 2026-09-11), 41 of 535 skill folders have more than 20 files (the largest is plugins/cloudflare/skills/cloudflare with 316). 167 contain non-markdown files other than agents/openai.yaml, such as .py, .json, .mjs, .png, .svg, .sh and .csv. Many of these plugins come from partners but are published in OpenAI's curated repo.
Source files saved to the scratchpad: build-skills.md, plugins-skills.md, plugins-mcp-server.md, api-tools-skills.md, blog-skills-shell.md and openai_plugins_skill_counts.txt, all under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-2048/52a1ea60-b7a7-54b2-835a-a72ec8f4e1e5/scratchpad/.

verify_anthropic.limit_claim_verdict: MOSTLY ACCURATE, with one clear omission and a few small points to add. The core claim holds: none of the listed sources sets a limit on how many files a skill folder can hold, and none requires files to be markdown only. I checked each source. The overview, best practices and skills-guide have no file-count limit. The Create Skill API reference (/docs/en/api/skills/create) says only that files is an array, that all files must be in one top-level directory with SKILL.md at its root, and that display_name is at most 255 characters. The Claude Code skills doc, the agentskills.io spec, the blog and skill-creator SKILL.md also have no file-count limit. The three quotes the claim relies on are word for word: 'may contain any files and directories beyond the required SKILL.md', 'No practical limit on bundled content' and 'unlimited'. These are also word for word: 'Maximum Skill upload size: 30 MB (all files combined, uncompressed)', 'Maximum Skills per request: 20' (it counts skills per API request, not files), the 64-character name and 1024-character description limits (spec, skills-guide, best practices), the 255-character display_name limit, the 1,536-character listing cap in Claude Code, SKILL.md under 500 lines (best practices, Claude Code docs, spec), the spec's '< 5000 tokens recommended', the overview's Level 2 'Under 5k tokens', a table of contents above 100 lines (best practices) or above 300 lines (skill-creator), and 'No network access' / 'No runtime package installation' for API skills. CORRECTIONS AND CAVEATS: (1) OMISSION: the claude.ai support article 'How to create custom skills' (support.claude.com/en/articles/12512198), which the claim says it checked, gives a stricter description limit: 'description: ... (200 characters maximum)' (and 'name: ... (64 characters maximum)'). The claim gives only the 1024-character limit and should also mention the 200-character limit claude.ai states. (2) On the claude.ai zip size: 'could not find' is accurate. That article gives no size limit, and neither does 'Use skills in Claude' (12512180). But 12512180 lists 'ZIP file exceeds size limits' among common upload failures, so a claude.ai limit exists without a published number. A web-search summary said '50 MB', but that figure is not in the current page text, so do not cite it. (3) The 1,536-character cap is a default that the skillListingMaxDescChars setting can change, so it is not fixed. (4) The Claude Code docs have one more runtime limit on skill content, though not on file count: after auto-compaction, each skill keeps its first 5,000 tokens, with 25,000 tokens combined across skills. None of these points changes the conclusion. No official source limits a skill to 20 files or to markdown files only.

verify_openai.limit_claim_verdict: MOSTLY ACCURATE. There are a few minor imprecisions in the self-computed counts, and one surface could not be checked. VERIFIED: (1) API limits of 500 files per version, a 50 MB zip and 25 MB uncompressed. They appear exactly as quoted on the live page. The doc doesn't say whether 25 MB is per file or per bundle. (2) The MCP import limits are exact: 100 files per skill; 256 KiB for SKILL.md; 1 MiB per supporting file; 5 MiB per skill; 8 MiB of archives per scan. The doc says 'up to five uniquely named skills across 10 catalog pages', so 'up to 5 skills per scan' is a fair paraphrase. (3) I read the whole live learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills page. It has no file-count or size limit. developers.openai.com/codex/skills does return a 308 to it. Small wording fix: the budget is 'at most 2% of the model's context window, or 8,000 characters when the context window is unknown'. So 8,000 is a fallback, not a second cap. The page also says this budget applies only to the initial list. (4) I read quick_validate.py and it is identical to the live raw GitHub file. It checks the frontmatter keys (name, description, license, allowed-tools, metadata), name ≤64 characters, description ≤1024 with no < or >, and nothing about file count or type. It also checks that SKILL.md exists, that the name is hyphen-case, and that name and description are present, so 'only the frontmatter' is slightly simplified. (5) The skill-creator soft guidance is confirmed verbatim: <500 lines, <5k words, 'Unlimited', one level deep, a table of contents for files over 100 lines, grep patterns for files over 10k words. (6) The openai/skills README deprecation notice is confirmed. It points to openai/plugins and to developers.openai.com/codex/plugins/build. The current docs (build-skills, plugins/build/skills) do repeat the scripts/references/assets structure. (7) The openai/plugins clone at 1dc1958 is the live HEAD (git ls-remote matches; commit date 2026-09-11). Its largest skill is plugins/cloudflare/skills/cloudflare with 316 files (confirmed). NUMERIC CAVEATS: '535' leaves out the repo's own .agents/skills/plugin-creator; there are 536 SKILL.md folders in total. '41 with more than 20 files' reproduces only when each parent folder's count includes the nested sub-skill folders inside it. 29 of the 535 folders are nested, for example the zoom meeting-sdk/windows sub-skill. Counting each skill's own files gives 35. '167 with non-markdown files' reproduces only if every openai.yaml, including nested sub-skills' copies, is excluded, or if nested folders aren't counted inside their parents. A strict recursive count that excludes only the top-level agents/openai.yaml gives 172. So the 41 and the 167 use different rules for nested folders. None of this weakens the conclusion that many skills exceed 20 files and hold non-markdown files. The listed file types (.py, .json, .mjs, .png, .svg, .sh, .csv) are all present. UNVERIFIED GAP: the ChatGPT workspace Skills help article (help.openai.com/en/articles/20001066-skills-in-chatgpt), which is linked from learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/skills, returned 403 to both WebFetch and curl. Search snippets show no skill-specific file-count limit there, only a general 512 MB per-file upload limit for ChatGPT. I could not rule out an upload limit for workspace Skills, so 'No official OpenAI source sets a 20-file cap' is well supported but not fully checked for that surface. I found no source that sets a 20-file cap or requires markdown-only files. Both OpenAI pages say SKILL.md is the only required file.
